column1: What is the core invariant governing all post-processing operations on 3D printed parts?
column2: Macro-scale mechanical properties emerge from molecular-scale architecture; every post-processing operation either reinforces or degrades that underlying architecture.

column1: Why do FDM parts exhibit anisotropic properties?
column2: The extrusion process aligns polymer chains preferentially along the print direction, creating interlayer interfaces with incomplete chain entanglement that remain the weakest structural planes throughout the part's life.

column1: What UV wavelength range triggers photopolymerization in resin printing, and what is the mechanism?
column2: 385–405 nm UV light causes the photoinitiator to generate free radicals, triggering a crosslinking cascade that transforms liquid monomer/oligomer into a solid polymer network.

column1: Why do cured photopolymer resins NOT soften predictably with heat like thermoplastics?
column2: Because resins are crosslinked thermosets formed by irreversible chemical reaction; instead of softening reversibly, they undergo irreversible thermal degradation when heated.

column1: What causes dimensional drift and surface tackiness in resin prints after they leave the printer?
column2: Incomplete curing leaves unreacted monomers trapped in the matrix, which continue to slowly cure (crosslink) over time, causing ongoing dimensional and surface changes.

column1: What formula governs the visibility of staircase artifacts on an FFF surface, and what do the variables mean?
column2: h_visible = L / cos(θ), where L is layer height and θ is the surface angle relative to the build plane.

column1: Why is PETG problematic for water-based smoothing compounds?
column2: PETG is hygroscopic, so water-based compounds get absorbed into the bulk material, compromising dimensional stability.

column1: What physical mechanism do abrasive finishing methods (sanding, tumbling, vapor honing) rely on to remove material?
column2: They fracture surface asperities through shear stress that exceeds the material's yield strength; removed material embeds in abrasive media, disperses in fluid, or accumulates as debris.

column1: What determines solvent penetration depth and compatibility during chemical vapor smoothing, per Flory-Huggins theory?
column2: The Flory-Huggins interaction parameter χ: a small χ means the solvent is thermodynamically compatible with the polymer, enabling rapid/uniform penetration; a large χ means incompatibility and minimal effect.

column1: What is the physical basis of annealing in semi-crystalline thermoplastics (e.g., PLA, PETG, PA12)?
column2: Heating below the melt point but above Tg restores chain mobility, allowing polymer chains to reorganize into lower-energy crystalline structures, increasing HDT and stiffness (e.g., PLA HDT can rise from ~55°C to over 100°C after annealing at 80–90°C for 90 min).

column1: Why does over-cured or improperly washed-out SLA resin become extremely brittle?
column2: Photopolymer over-cure or incomplete monomer washout drives the glass transition temperature (Tg) too high, eliminating the material's ability to yield under load.

column1: What causes warping in FDM printed parts, root cause?
column2: Asynchronous cooling and volumetric contraction: upper layers cool and shrink while already-solidified lower layers remain anchored to the bed, generating internal tensile stress that exceeds bed adhesion or interlayer strength.
